title: Peppermint foot balm
subtitle: A cooling, thick balm for dry heels and tired feet
excerpt: A thick beeswax-and-shea balm scented with peppermint essential oil. The peppermint gives a cooling sensation on tired, hot feet. Higher beeswax percentage than a regular balm for a firmer stick that stays in place. Gives about 120 g of balm. Shelf life 12 months.
sourceNotes: Foot balm formulation: higher beeswax percentage (30%) than a face or hand balm for a firmer product suitable for elbows and heels. Shea butter adds creaminess and emollience. Coconut oil adds antimicrobial properties. Peppermint EO (Mentha piperita): menthol activates cold receptors (TRPM8) producing the characteristic cooling sensation without temperature change. Safe for external use; avoid in children under 2 and on the face. Max 6% for foot-use balms under IFRA guidelines. This recipe uses 3%.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles cleanly. Pour into one large 250 ml tin or two 125 ml tins.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use once set (2 hours). Keeps 12 months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 12 months in a cool place. Anhydrous; no preservative needed. Discard if the balm smells rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: Menthol, the main constituent of peppermint essential oil, activates cold-sensitive receptors in the skin, producing a cooling sensation without any actual change in skin temperature.
A preparation with no water phase. Anhydrous balms need no preservative because there is no moisture for micro-organisms to grow in.

makes it particularly useful for hot, tired feet after a long day. The higher beeswax ratio produces a firmer texture than a face or hand balm, so it stays where it's applied. About 120 g of balm; keeps 12 months.

content.text: Combine the beeswax, shea butter, coconut oil, and castor oil in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Stir until the beeswax is completely melted.
Remove from heat. Cool to 40°C, then stir in the peppermint essential oil. Peppermint contains menthol, which partly evaporates if added to very hot oil.
Pour into the tin and leave undisturbed for 2 hours until fully set.
balm keeps 12 months at room temperature. The cooling effect fades first (menthol is the most volatile component); the balm itself remains usable until the oils smell rancid.
